options.swap: Wild fermentation, the batter or dough's own yeasts and bacteria
options.ratio: No 1:1. Replace 2 tsp yeast with 8–12 hours at 28–32°C, or a 1/4 cup mature starter.
options.taste_and_texture: Sourer, more complex, and much less predictable. It will fail on a cold night. That is the trade.
options.nutritional_rationale: A long ferment loosens the grip the grain keeps on its own iron and calcium, so more of what is in the flour reaches the plate. Slower is doing the work, not the organism.

options.swap: Curd or buttermilk as a starter
options.ratio: 2 tbsp thick curd per cup of batter, left 6–8 hours warm.
options.taste_and_texture: Reliably tangy, faster than a pure wild ferment, less lift.
options.nutritional_rationale: The same gain on iron and calcium, in a shorter ferment.

where_it_went: Commercial yeast made leavening fast and repeatable, which is exactly what bakeries and packaged bread needed; the ambient overnight ferment became a weekend project.
